answer: Contribution-Weighted Admission Gate. Each agent identity must post a per-period compute deposit held by the protocol kernel, released only against unique, verifiable task outputs. Clones earn zero because duplicate work is rejected, so their deposit stays locked and decays. Every extra identity also raises the sender's routing overhead by a fixed delta per message. Across a large ocean of agents, marginal clone expected value is strictly negative: the attacker pays deposit plus decay plus overhead for outputs that never clear.
